title: When updating  "launcher" property of Task Manager from JS scripting api, effects are not visible until restarting plasmashell
line: Setting Task Manager launchers from a desktop script now shows the new launchers right away instead of a blank one until restart.
explanation: The scripting API's writeConfig() put the raw JavaScript value straight into the widget's config item, but also wrote it to the config file. For a list key like the Task Manager's launchers, a comma-separated string became a one-element list at runtime (one blank launcher), while the file kept the string that KConfig later splits into a proper list, so only a restart showed the right launchers. writeConfig() now writes the value to the file first and sets the item from the file through KConfig's type conversion, so the live value matches what a restart reads.

commits.message:
shell/scripting: give the widget the value writeConfig writes to the file

writeConfig() gave the raw script value to the widget, so a string with
commas for a list key became one bogus entry until a restart parsed the
file. The value is now written first and read back with the item's type.

BUG: 446739

media.caption: Master: after the report's script sets launchers to "dolphin,konsole" as one string, the panel shows a single blank launcher.
With the fix: the same script shows the Dolphin and Konsole launchers immediately.

review.text: This fixes the real cause: writeConfig() gave the raw JS value to the skeleton item but wrote it to the file too, so the live value and the value read after a restart differed for list keys. Writing first and reading back through KConfig with the item's type makes both go through the same conversion. It is a 3-line change, and the regression checks covered array, bool and int keys. The screenshots show one blank launcher before and the right launchers after.
